title: Two orchestras breathe the same melody
question: How do Stokowski and Monteux make room for the opening melody’s long phrases?
intro: Stokowski recorded the Philadelphia Orchestra on 12 November 1934; Monteux’s San Francisco recording dates from 3–4 March 1942. The comparison uses Stokowski’s first disc side against the opening of Monteux’s complete movement. Alignment is restricted to the inspected opening phrases, Stokowski 2.8–65 seconds and Monteux 2.2–42 seconds; later music and whole-movement speed comparisons are excluded.
